Command: Do not anoint a stranger with the holy anointing oil
Summary: The command: Do not anoint a stranger with the holy anointing oil (Exodus 30:32). The holy anointing oil was poured on Aaron and his sons and on the tabernacle alone, never on an outsider.
Commandment: Do not anoint a stranger with the holy anointing oil.
Application: This row narrows the parent group command to this one mitzvah. The moral/ceremonial/civil division is a traditional classification, not Scripture's own division; this law is traditionally classed as ceremonial. Hebrews teaches the earthly tabernacle was a copy of the heavenly one, and Christ now serves as high priest in the true tabernacle.
Purpose: To give Israel a mediated approach to God through the tabernacle pattern (Exodus 25:40). Hebrews teaches the earthly copy gave way to Christ's priesthood in the true tabernacle (Hebrews 8:1-6).
Function: The holy anointing oil was poured on Aaron and his sons and on the tabernacle alone, never on an outsider — a ceremonial law of restricted anointing. Its goal was to keep the anointing where God put it: on the priests and the sanctuary, and nowhere else. The evil was spreading the holy oil beyond its appointment, treating consecration as something to hand out freely. It restrained that by the ban: the stranger was not anointed, and the oil stayed holy.
